title: My Calendar II
description:
Your calendar now tolerates some overlap: two events may share time, but three may not. Each event is the half-open range `[start, end)`, covering every `t` with `start <= t < end`. A *triple booking* happens when some moment is covered by three events at once. Events that only touch at an endpoint do not overlap.

Implement the `MyCalendarTwo` class:

- `MyCalendarTwo()` creates an empty calendar.
- `boolean book(int start, int end)` tries to add the event `[start, end)`. If adding it would not create a triple booking, store it and return `true`. Otherwise leave the calendar unchanged and return `false`.

Rejected events are never stored.

The input lists the operation names and their argument lists. The output lists each call's return value, using `null` for the constructor.

**Example 1:**
```
Input: ["MyCalendarTwo","book","book","book","book","book","book"], [[],[10,20],[50,60],[10,40],[5,15],[5,10],[25,55]]
Output: [null,true,true,true,false,true,true]
Explanation: [10,40) double-books [10,20). [5,15) would cover [10,15) a third time, so it is rejected. [5,10) only touches [10,20) and [10,40) at 10, so it is accepted. [25,55) double-books [25,40) and [50,55) but never triples.
```

**Example 2:**
```
Input: ["MyCalendarTwo","book","book","book","book"], [[],[1,5],[2,6],[3,4],[5,7]]
Output: [null,true,true,false,true]
Explanation: [1,5) and [2,6) overlap on [2,5). [3,4) falls inside that double-booked region, so it is rejected. [5,7) overlaps only [2,6), on [5,6).
```

**Example 3:**
```
Input: ["MyCalendarTwo","book","book","book","book"], [[],[0,10],[0,10],[0,10],[10,20]]
Output: [null,true,true,false,true]
Explanation: The same slot can be booked twice but not a third time. [10,20) only touches the existing events.
```

examples.explanation: [10,40) double-books [10,20). [5,15) would cover [10,15) a third time, so it is rejected. [5,10) only touches [10,20) and [10,40) at 10, so it is accepted. [25,55) double-books [25,40) and [50,55) but never triples.
[1,5) and [2,6) overlap on [2,5). [3,4) falls inside that double-booked region, so it is rejected. [5,7) overlaps only [2,6), on [5,6).
The same slot can be booked twice but not a third time. [10,20) only touches the existing events.

constraints: At most 1000 calls will be made to book
solution_approach: A brute force recomputes coverage for every request: for each candidate moment (all event endpoints) count how many stored events plus the new one cover it, rejecting on any count of 3; this is O(n^2) per call. The standard optimal-for-constraints approach keeps two lists: all accepted bookings, and the double-booked overlaps among them. For a request [s, e), first reject if it overlaps any interval in the overlaps list (that would be a triple). Otherwise, for every accepted booking that overlaps [s, e), append the intersection [max(s, x), min(e, y)) to the overlaps list, then store the booking. Each call is O(n) and total space is O(n). An alternative is a sweep-line difference map (TreeMap of +1/-1 at endpoints) that checks the running count stays below 3, at O(n) per call, or a segment tree with lazy max for O(log C) per call.
hints: A triple booking can only happen where the new event lands on a region that is already double-booked.
Track two collections: the accepted events, and the regions where two accepted events overlap.
For [s, e): if it intersects any double-booked region, return false. Otherwise add its intersection with every accepted event, [max(s, x), min(e, y)), to the double-booked list and store it.
follow_up_questions: How would you generalise this to allow at most k overlapping events (My Calendar III style)?
How could a segment tree with lazy propagation make each booking O(log C)?
